note: learned by hand-moving the axes; read-only, no motor was commanded

1.note: raw units are motor-side (4096 = 360 deg, multi-turn, relative). Use calibration/limits to convert to robot yaw.

calibration.method: hand-set -90 and +90 degrees of the yaw axis, motor position read at each (read-only)
calibration.accuracy: only as good as how exactly the +/-90 positions were set by hand; verify with a third point

front_history.note: set by the user: "this is front" after the motor lost power (the raw origin changes when the motor is power-cycled)

limits.source: min and max given by the user, read from the motor while hand-set at each end

safe.note: self-imposed limits (physical range +/-90; the motor itself allows ~69 deg/s of robot yaw = its 73 rpm Velocity Limit register). 60 deg/s of robot yaw = about 383 deg/s (~64 rpm) at the motor: matches the scenarios (yaw <= 60 deg/s). Raise only step by step.

record.how: learned by hand-moving the axis; read-only, no motor was commanded

calibration.how: user held the tilt level for 10 s; median of the readings (read-only)
calibration.note: motor-side numbers. Gear / linkage ratio to the real tilt angle is still unknown (needs a known second angle).

anchors.meaning: level, held by hand for 10 s

calibration.mapping: piecewise linear through the three anchors; +deg = up = raw decreasing
calibration.assumption: the learned end stops are +15 / -15 deg of robot tilt (set by the user, not measured with an angle gauge)

safe.note: tilt: +/-13 deg (the taught ends are +/-15). 30 deg/s of robot tilt = about 36 deg/s (~6 rpm) at the motor. Raise only step by step.
